rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ‘Heart’ means intellect, as in asking where someone's heart went; a person who does not grasp the reminder is as though heartless.
rows.anchor: معنى القلب هنا العقل عن ابن عباس من قولهم أين ذهب قلبك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, the heart is a living heart.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لمن كان له قلب حي عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: To cast one's hearing is to listen without distraction, present to and understanding what is heard, rather than inattentive or forgetful.
rows.anchor: وهو شهيد لما يسمع فيفقهه غير غافل عنه ولا ساه عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, the witness is a person from the People of the Book who recognizes the Prophet's description in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: هو شهيد على صفة النبي في الكتب السالفة يريد أهل الكتاب عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says creation of the heavens and earth caused no weariness, refuting Jews who claimed that God rested on the Sabbath and therefore did no work then.
rows.anchor: أكذب الله تعالى بهذا اليهود فإنهم قالوا استراح الله يوم السبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to endure their slander and lies, including calling him a sorcerer or madman, until God brings relief; this was before fighting was commanded.
rows.anchor: من بهتهم وكذبهم وقولهم إنك ساحر أو مجنون واحتمل ذلك حتى يأتي الله بالفرج وهذا قبل أن أمر الله بالقتال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: ‘Glorify with praise’ means pray and praise God, since prayer includes glorification and praise.
rows.anchor: أي وصل واحمد الله تعالى سمى الصلاة تسبيحا لأن الصلاة تشتمل على التسبيح والتحميد عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is verbal glorification of God, declaring Him above what is unworthy of Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به التسبيح بالقول تنزيها لله تعالى عما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: The times before sunrise and sunset refer to the dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: يعني صلاة الفجر وصلاة الظهر والعصر عن قتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The night prayer includes the sunset and late evening prayers.
rows.anchor: ومن الليل يعني صلاة الليل ويدخل فيه صلاة المغرب والعشاء عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: He prescribed saying the declaration of God's oneness ten times morning and evening.
rows.anchor: تقول حين تصبح وحين تمسي عشر مرات لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والحسن بن علي والحسن والشعبي وابن عباس
rows.claim: ‘After prostrations’ means two rakʿahs after sunset, while ‘after the stars’ means two before dawn; Ibn Abbas transmits the view from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به الركعتان بعد المغرب وأدبار النجوم الركعتان قبل الفجر عن علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Another view takes ‘after prostrations’ as glorification after every obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: أنه التسبيح بعد كل صلاة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد والجبائي
rows.claim: Another interpretation is voluntary prayers performed after obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: أنه النوافل بعد المفروضات عن ابن زيد والجبائي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A further interpretation identifies it with the witr prayer at the end of the night.
rows.anchor: أنه الوتر من آخر الليل روي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: The Kufans other than Asim read the noun in the singular, while the remaining readers use the plural.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم بموقع النجوم بغير ألف والباقون بمواقع النجوم على الجمع

rows.speaker: بعضهم عن عاصم
rows.claim: Some transmit from Asim a light form of the verb ‘you deny’; the well-known reading is intensive.
rows.anchor: وروى بعضهم عن عاصم أنكم تكذبون بالتخفيف والقراءة المشهورة بالتشديد

rows.speaker: الحسن والثقفي
rows.claim: An anomalous reading has ‘so I swear’ without the alif.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة الحسن والثقفي فلا قسم بخير ألف

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس والنبي
rows.claim: A reported alternative reads that they make their gratitude into denial.
rows.anchor: قراءة علي ع وابن عباس ورويت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He explains the oath as an actual oath and the stars' locations as their settings, where they disappear.
rows.anchor: أي فاقسم ومواقعها مساقطها حيث تغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes the locations those of Quranic revelation as it descended to the Prophet in successive portions.
rows.anchor: قال: غيره: إنه مواقع القرآن حين نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نجوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural can be used for a verbal noun because its instances differ; the singular is a generic noun.
rows.anchor: فإن المصادر وسائر الأجناس إذا اختلفت جاز جمعها ومن قرأ بموقع فأفرد فلأنه اسم جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the light reading, they deny that God alone gave the provision, attributing it instead to a star's rising.
rows.anchor: فتقولون مطرنا بنوء كذا فهذا وجه التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the intensive reading, their attribution of provision to another source denies the Quran's teaching that God provides it.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أنكم تكذبون بالقرآن لأن الله تعالى هو الذي رزقكم ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: ‘Making gratitude denial’ means replacing the gratitude owed for provision with denial; Ibn Jinni also parses it as taking denial in place of gratitude.
rows.anchor: هو على وتجعلون بدل شكركم ومثله قول العجاج

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: His line about being repaid with a stick witnesses the word ‘instead’ in the alternative grammatical construction.
rows.anchor: ربيته حتى إذا تمعددا كان جزائي بالعصا أن أجلدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath means ‘I do swear’ in the present; Quranic oaths are present, whereas a future oath would require the emphatic nūn, so the negating particle is extra.
rows.anchor: التقدير لأنا أقسم وهو فعل الحال يدل على ذلك أن جميع ما في القرآن من الأقسام إنما هو حاضر الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath is a clause that confirms a report by placing it among what is true rather than false.
rows.anchor: القسم جملة من الكلام يؤكد بها الخبر بما يجعله في قسم الصواب دون الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Great’ describes one whose measure surpasses what can be measured in another; it can mean physical or honorific greatness.
rows.anchor: والعظيم هو الذي يقصر مقدار ما يكون من غيره عما يكون منه وهو ضربان عظيم الشخص وعظيم الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is truly noble because its proofs yield abundant good and lead to truth; God's attribute of noble giver is eternal.
rows.anchor: فلما كان القرآن من شأنه أن يعطي الخير الكثير بأدلته المؤدية إلى الحق كان كريما على حقيقة معنى الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hypocritical ‘oiler’ is one whose inward conduct contradicts outward appearance, moving smoothly into it like oil.
rows.anchor: والمدهن الذي يجري في الباطن على خلاف الظاهر كالدهن في سهولة ذلك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Recompense’ is the meaning of dīn, as in the saying that one is repaid as one repays; it can also mean the deed deserving recompense.
rows.anchor: والدين هو الجزاء ومنه قولهم كما تدين تدان أي كما تجزي تجزى والدين العمل الذي يستحق به الجزاء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The reward is the recompense for obedience and the light of faith that guides believers on the road to Paradise; al-Baraʾ transmits this from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي لهم ثواب طاعاتهم ونور إيمانهم الذي يهتدون به إلى طريق الجنة وهذا قول عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: منهال القصاب
rows.claim: When Minhal asked Abu Abdillah to pray for martyrdom, he answered that a believer is a martyr and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قلت لأبي عبد الله ع: ادع الله أن يرزقني الشهادة فقال: إن المؤمن شهيد وقرأ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الحارث بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar compared one who awaits and hopes for good from the family of Muhammad's Qaʾim to a fighter alongside him, then to a fighter and martyr alongside the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ثم قال الثالثة بل والله كمن استشهد مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في فسطاطه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومسروق ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: The phrase ‘the witnesses’ begins a new clause and means prophets who testify for and against their communities; al-Farraʾ and al-Zajjaj selected this interpretation.
rows.anchor: إن الشهداء منفصل مما قبله مستأنف والمراد بالشهداء الأنبياء ع الذين يشهدون للأمم وعليهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان وابن جرير
rows.claim: An alternative takes the witnesses as those killed in God's path.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم الذين استشهدوا في سبيل الله عن مقاتل بن سليمان وابن جرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is like play and amusement because it quickly vanishes without permanence.
rows.anchor: أي بمنزلة اللهو واللعب إذ لا بقاء لذلك ولا دوام ويزول عن وشيك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Every form of play is amusement.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كل لعب لهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, play is what people desire in worldly life and amusement is what distracts them from the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللعب ما رغب في الدنيا واللهو ما ألهى عن الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment is what people decorate themselves with, or the world's appearance that delights its people before disappearing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بذلك أنها تتحلى في أعين أهلها ثم تتلاشى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: People boast of worldly things to their peers and neighbors.
rows.anchor: يفاخِر الرجل بها قرينه وجاره عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People exhaust their lives collecting wealth, children, and servants for rivalry and to lord those advantages over God's friends.
rows.anchor: ويتطاول على أولياء الله بماله وولده وخدمه والمعنى أنه يفني عمره في هذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: ‘Farmers’ is a possible sense of kāfir here, since they cultivate and cover seed; alternatively the word means unbelievers, who delight more in worldly life.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون المراد الكفار بالله لأن الكافر أشد إعجابا بالدنيا من غيره

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The severe punishment in the hereafter is for God's enemies, while forgiveness and approval are for His friends and obedient people.
rows.anchor: عذاب شديد } لأعداء الله عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Worldly life is deceptive provision for whoever neglects the afterlife; for one who seeks it, worldly life is a provision carrying him to something better.
rows.anchor: متاع الغرور لمن لم يشتغل بطلب الآخرة ومن اشتغل بطلبها فهي له متاع بلاغ إلى ما هو خير منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes worldly activity itself deceptive provision, ephemeral like the stages of plant growth in the parable.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه والعمل للحياة الدنيا متاع الغرور وأنه كهذه الأشياء التي مثل بها في الزوال والفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's ‘tomorrow’ is the Day of Resurrection; each person should inspect what they sent ahead, good deeds that save or bad deeds that ruin them.
rows.anchor: يعني ليوم القيامة والمعنى لينظر كل امرئ ما الذي قدمه لنفسه أعملا صالحا ينجيه أم سيئا يوبقه ويرديه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God made the Hour seem as near as tomorrow to prompt reflection on what people have prepared.
rows.anchor: إن ربكم قرب الساعة حتى جعلها كغد وأمركم بالتدبر والتفكر فيما قدمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ghad is originally ghadw, but the Quran always omits its wāw; poetry shows both the omitted and retained forms.
rows.anchor: أصل غد غدو إلا أنه لم يأت في القرآن إلا محذوف الواو وجاء في الشعر بحذف الواو وإثباتها

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: The line about people being like dwellings witnesses poetic use of ghad without the wāw.
rows.anchor: وما الناس إلا كالديار وأهلها بها يوم حلوها وغدوا بلاقع

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: The line urging not to drive a camel and lower a bucket witnesses poetic use of ghad with the wāw.
rows.anchor: لا تقلواها وادلواها دلوا إن مع اليوم أخاها غدوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The parable's human is an Israelite worshipper named Barsisa, whom Satan gradually led into fornication, murder, and finally apostasy at execution.
rows.anchor: عابد بني إسرائيل عن ابن عباس قال: إنه كان في بني إسرائيل عابد اسمه برصيصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story parallels Banu Nadir, who were deceived by hypocrites and then abandoned when danger came.
rows.anchor: ضرب الله هذه القصة لبني النضير حين اغتروا بالمنافقين ثم تبرأوا منهم عند الشدة وأسلموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view relates the parable to Badr: Satan urged fighting the Messenger, then fled when he saw the angels and said he feared God.
rows.anchor: يوم بدر إذ دعا إلى حرب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما رأى الملائكة رجع القهقهرى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Alternatively, Satan and the human are generic: Satan always calls people to disbelief, then disowns them when needed; he says he fears God on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أراد بالشيطان والإنسان اسم الجنس لا المعهود فإن الشيطان أبدا يدعو الإنسان إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two who end in Hell are both the tempter and those he misled among hypocrites and Jews; that is the recompense of wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: يعني عاقبة الفريقين الداعي والمدعو من الشيطان ومن أغواه من المنافقين واليهود أنهما معذبان في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first command to fear God urges repentance for past sins; the second guards against future sins.
rows.anchor: إنما كرر الأمر بالتقوى لأن الأولى للتوبة عما مضى من الذنوب والثانية لاتقاء المعاصي في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the repeated command to fear God simply reinforces the first.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الثانية تأكيد للأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who forget God fail to fulfill His due, so God makes them lose their share of good and reward.
rows.anchor: أي تركوا أداء حق الله

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Alternatively, they forget God by abandoning gratitude and reverence, and God makes them forget themselves through punishment; ‘yourselves’ can mean one another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نسوا الله بترك ذكره بالشكر والتعظيم فأنساهم أنفسهم بالعذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The people meant by those who forgot God are Banu Qurayza, Banu Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa.
rows.anchor: ويريد به بني قريظة وبني النضير وبني قينقاع عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors are those who have left obedience to God for disobedience.
rows.anchor: الذين خرجوا من طاعة الله إلى معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of Hell and Paradise are unequal because the former deserve Hell and the latter deserve Paradise; Paradise's people attain God's reward.
rows.anchor: أي لا يتساويان لأن هؤلاء يستحقون النار وأولئك يستحقون الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads ‘and I would be’ with the subjunctive; the other readers use the jussive form.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو { وأكون } بالنصب والباقون وأكن بالجزم

rows.speaker: حماد ويحيى
rows.claim: Hammad and Yahya read ‘what they do’ in the third person; the other readers address the audience directly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حماد ويحيى { بما يعملون } بالياء والباقون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jussive ‘and I be’ coordinates with the implied jussive condition after ‘if only you delayed me’; the request implies ‘if you delay me, I will give charity.’
rows.anchor: وقد أغنى السؤال عن ذكر الشرط والتقدير أخرني فإنك إن تؤخرني أصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr follows the visible subjunctive after the fāʾ, a preferable construction because the overt form is clear and close; a codex of Ubayy reportedly has both verbs in that form.
rows.anchor: وأما قول أبي عمرو وأكون فإنما حمله على اللفظ دون الموضع وكان الحمل على اللفظ أولى لظهوره في اللفظ وقربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jussive can follow a conditional answer whose fāʾ and following words are understood, as in the cited Quranic parallel and two poetic examples.
rows.anchor: ويذرهم لما كان فلا هادي له في موضع فعل مجزوم حمل ويذرهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person reading treats ‘a soul’ as plural in meaning despite its singular form; the second-person reading is a general address.
rows.anchor: لأن النفس وإن كان واحدا في اللفظ فالمراد به الكثرة ومن قرأ بالتاء كان خطابا شائعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infidād means dispersal; silver is named for its distribution in the prices of purchased things, and anything distracting one from another thing is called a diversion.
rows.anchor: الانفضاض التفرق وفض الكتاب إذا فرقه ونشره وسميت الفضة فضة لتفرقها في أثمان الأشياء المشتراة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: His line about a poem distracting the sons of Jusham from every virtue supplies an example of the verb ‘to distract.’
rows.anchor: ألهى بني جشم عن كل مكرمة قصيدة قالها عمرو بن كلثوم

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: His line about distracting a pregnant woman and nursing mother also witnesses the meaning of ‘to distract.’
rows.anchor: فمثلك حبلى قد طرقت ومرضع فألهيتها عن ذي تمائم محول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura's occasion is the expedition against Banu al-Mustaliq, when Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions stirred dissension after the Muslims defeated and captured them.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أبي المنافق وأصحابه وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the watering place, Jahjah al-Ghifari and Sinan al-Juhani fought and each called on his own group, prompting supporters to rally by Emigrant and Helper identity.
rows.anchor: فازدحم جهجاه وسنان الجهني من بني عوف بن خزرج على الماء فاقتتلا فصرخ الجهني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaʿal spoke sharply to Abdullah, who threatened harm in anger.
rows.anchor: واشتد لسان جعال على عبد الله فقال عبد الله والذي يحلف به لأزرنك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Ubayy complained that the migrants had multiplied in Medina, argued against sharing food with them, and said his faction would expel the Messenger on returning.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن أبي قد نافرونا وكاثرونا في بلادنا والله ما مثلنا ومثلهم إلا كما قال القائل

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: Zayd rebuked Abdullah as despised and weak among his people, while Muhammad was honored by God and loved by Muslims.
rows.anchor: فقال زيد بن أرقم أنت والله الذليل القليل المبغض في قومك ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في عز من الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet questioned Abdullah, he denied the remarks; Helpers defended their elder and suggested Zayd may have erred.
rows.anchor: والذي أنزل عليك الكتاب ما قلت شيئا من ذلك قط

rows.speaker: أسيد بن الحضير
rows.claim: Usayd said the Prophet could expel Abdullah, but urged gentle treatment because Abdullah and his people had once planned to crown him.
rows.anchor: فقال أسيد: فأنت والله يا رسول الله تخرجه إن شئت هو والله الذليل وأنت العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Ubayy son offered to carry out his father execution rather than risk killing a believer in revenge; the Prophet told him to treat his father gently.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن عبد الله بن أبي ما كان من أمر أبيه فأتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله إنه قد بلغني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet kept the army moving through the day, night, and following morning to distract people from Abdullah ibn Ubayy scandalous remarks.
rows.anchor: وسار رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالناس يومهم ذلك حتى أمسى وليلتهم حتى أصبح وصدر يومهم ذلك حتى آذتهم الشمس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the camel was lost, the Prophet said a great hypocrite had died in Medina; he named Rifaʿa, who was then found to have died that day.
rows.anchor: وضلت ناقة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك ليلا فقال مات اليوم منافق عظيم النفاق

rows.speaker: منافق
rows.claim: A hypocrite mocked the Prophet claim to know where the camel was; Gabriel then informed the Prophet of both the insult and the camel location, which proved correct.
rows.anchor: كيف يزعم أنه يعلم الغيب ولا يعلم مكان ناقته ألا يخبره الذي يأتيه بالوحي

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: Zayd says the sura was revealed on their return, confirming his report and exposing Abdullah as a liar; the Prophet praised his truthful mouth, hearing, and heart.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن أرقم فلما وافى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة جلست في البيت لما بي من الهم والحياء فنزلت سورة المنافقين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: The son blocked his father from entering Medina until the Prophet allowed him through, demonstrating who was honored and who was lowly.
rows.anchor: ما لك ويلك قال والله لا تدخلها إلا بإذن رسول الله ولتعلمن اليوم من الأعز ومن الأذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After only a few days Abdullah became ill and died; when told to seek the Prophet forgiveness, he refused and said that he had already believed and paid zakat.
rows.anchor: فلوى رأسه ثم قال أمرتموني أن أؤمن فقد آمنت وأمرتموني أن أعطي زكاة مالي فقد أعطيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness for them or not is equal, because they conceal disbelief while displaying belief, so God will not forgive them and will not guide people who depart from faith.
rows.anchor: أي يتساوى الاستغفار لهم وعدم الاستغفار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: God informed the Prophet that the hypocrites would die as unbelievers; his earlier requests for forgiveness were based on their outward appearance and the condition of genuine repentance, which hidden disbelief defeats.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: أخبره سبحانه أنهم يموتون على الكفر فلم يستغفر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites said not to support needy believers around the Messenger until they disperse; God owns all provision and tests believers with poverty so they can patiently earn reward.
rows.anchor: { ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض } وما بينهما من الأرزاق والأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the hypocrites fail to understand that God can bring about anything simply by commanding it to be.
rows.anchor: لا يفقهون أن أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls Muhammad His Messenger, rather than merely their companion, to honor and exalt him.
rows.anchor: ولكن الله سبحانه سماه رسول الله تشريفا له وتعظيما لقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘honored’ hypocrites meant themselves and the ‘lowly’ person meant the Messenger and believers; God answers that honor belongs to Him, His Messenger, and believers through divine support.
rows.anchor: فرد الله سبحانه عليهم بأن قال { ولله العزة ولرسوله } بإعلاء الله كلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation assigns glory by rank: lordship to God, prophethood to His Messenger, and servitude to believers; God later confirmed this by giving them victory and dominion.
rows.anchor: ولله العزة بالربوبية ولرسوله بالنبوة وللمؤمنين بالعبودية أخبر سبحانه بذلك ثم حققه بأن أعز رسوله والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further report enumerates five kinds of God's glory: sovereignty and permanence, majesty, giving, exalted rank, and splendor.
rows.anchor: عز الله خمسة عز الملك والبقاء وعز العظمة والكبرياء وعز البذل والعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger's five honors are precedence, the call to prayer, precedence among prophets, election, and triumph over enemies.
rows.anchor: وعز الرسول خمسة عز السبق والابتداء وعز الآذان والنداء وعز قدم الصدق على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers have five honors: being last yet first, ease, glad tidings, esteem, and numerical prominence; cited verses illustrate the first four.
rows.anchor: وعز التكثير بيانه أنهم أكثر الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's honor is the source of the Messenger's and believers' honor, so all honor ultimately belongs to God.
rows.anchor: أن عز الرسول والمؤمنين من جهته عز اسمه وإنما يحصل به وبطاعته فلله العز بأجمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children must not distract believers from the five prescribed prayers.
rows.anchor: أي عن الصلوات الخمس المفروضة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Alternatively, remembrance of God covers all forms of obedience.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله جميع طاعاته عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is remembering God's gifts with gratitude, meeting affliction with patience, and accepting His decree, in both hardship and blessing.
rows.anchor: ذكره شكره على نعمائه والصبر على بلائه والرضا بقضائه وهو إشارة إلى أنه لا ينبغي أن يغفل المؤمن عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever is distracted by wealth or children loses God's reward and mercy.
rows.anchor: من يشغله ماله وولده عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spend in good causes before death, including zakat and all other obligatory rights; death's signs prompt a futile wish for a short reprieve to give and become righteous.
rows.anchor: في سبيل البر فيدخل فيه الزكوات وسائر الحقوق الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is the strongest warning against neglecting God's rights; ‘righteous’ can mean those who perform good deeds.
rows.anchor: قالوا وليس في الزجر عن التفريط في حقوق الله آية أعظم من هذه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: One view says the verse addresses hypocrites.
rows.anchor: والآية في المنافقين عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view says it addresses believers, and ‘righteous’ means obedient people; Ibn Abbas says anyone who died with wealth but withheld zakat or could make pilgrimage but failed would ask to return, and here ‘righteousness’ means pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: ما من أحد يموت وكان له مال فلم يؤد زكاته وأطاق الحج فلم يحج

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The explanation that ‘righteous’ means pilgrimage is also transmitted from Abu Abdillah.
rows.anchor: قال الصلاح هنا الحج وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fixed term is the absolute time God decrees for a living person to die; a conditional term may be extended, shortened, or interrupted according to the benefit God knows.
rows.anchor: الأجل المطلق الذي حكم بأن الحي يموت عنده والأجل المقيد هو الأجل المحكوم بأن العبد يموت عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects to what precedes it: God would extend people's term if He knew they would repent, but He knows they will not.
rows.anchor: لو علم أنكم تتوبون لجعل في أجلكم تأخيرا إلى وقت آخر ولكنه علم أنكم لا تتوبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Gathering is Judgment Day, when earlier and later peoples are assembled for resurrection and requital.
rows.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة أي ذلك البعث والجزاء يكون في يوم يجمع فيه خلق الأولين والآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghubn is an exchange in which someone takes the worse and leaves the better, or takes the better and leaves the worse: believers give up worldly share for the afterlife, while unbelievers choose the reverse and are cheated.
rows.anchor: وهو تفاعل من الغبن وهو أخذ شر وترك خير أو أخذ خير وترك شر

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Day of Mutual Loss is when the people of Paradise outgain the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: يوم التغابن غبن أهل الجنة أهل النار عن قتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said each believer is shown the place in Hell they would have occupied had they done wrong, increasing gratitude; each person in Hell sees their lost place in Paradise, increasing regret.
rows.anchor: ما من عبد مؤمن يدخل الجنة إلا أري مقعده من النار لو أساء ليزداد شكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and righteous deeds cause God to erase sins and admit people to eternally flowing gardens; this is unsurpassed success.
rows.anchor: ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disbelieve and deny God's proofs remain in Hell, an evil destination.
rows.anchor: وبئس المصير } أي المآل والمرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men must not harm divorced women through deficient housing, maintenance, or clothing in order to force them out.
rows.anchor: لا تدخلوا الضرر عليهن بالتقصير في السكنى والنفقة والكسوة طالبين بالإضرار التضييق عليهن ليخرجن

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Alternatively, provide a dwelling adequate for sitting, sleeping, and washing; do not make it so constricted that she cannot live there.
rows.anchor: أعطوهن من المسكن ما يكفيهن لجلوسهن ومبيتهن وطهارتهن ولا تضايقوهن حتى يتعذر عليهن السكنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pregnant divorced woman must receive support until delivery because her waiting period ends with childbirth, whether the divorce is revocable or final.
rows.anchor: أمر الله سبحانه بالإنفاق على المطلقة الحامل سواء كانت رجعية أو مبتوتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the mother nurses the child after final separation, the father must pay the standard wage.
rows.anchor: فأعطوهن أجر الرضاع يعني أجرة المثل

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: The root of mutual consultation means discussing with one another; he cites the usage ‘they consult you.’
rows.anchor: أصله التشاور ومنه يأتمرون بك أي يتشاورون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers taking the command as planning fairly for the child and respecting the mother's care, without harming the father's means, the child's welfare, or normal nursing and wages; if they cannot agree, another woman may nurse.
rows.anchor: والأقوى عندي أن يكون المعنى دبروا بالمعروف بينكم في أمر الولد ومراعاة أمه

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: The line about what a man plans ultimately harming him witnesses the sense of deliberating or devising in the root of mutual consultation.
rows.anchor: أحار بن عمرو كأني خمر ويعدو على المرء ما يأتمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will bring ease after hardship, wealth after poverty, and relief after difficulty; this consoled impoverished Companions before later conquests.
rows.anchor: أي بعد ضيق سعة وبعد فقر غنى وبعد صعوبة الأمر سهولة وفي هذا تسلية للصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many towns' people rebelled against God and His messengers, so God scrutinized them, exacting what was due, and punished them with a terrible, unprecedented punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني جاوزوا الحد في العصيان والمخالفة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God reckoned with their deeds in worldly life by punishing them with annihilation.
rows.anchor: حاسبها الله تعالى بعملها في الدنيا فجازاها بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations make the terrible punishment the future Fire, put worldly famine, drought, sword, and calamities before the later reckoning, or define severe reckoning as one with no pardon.
rows.anchor: هو عذاب النار فإن اللفظ ماض بمعنى المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disastrous outcome was the ruin of unbelief in this life and the next; the next verse's severe punishment is Fire, showing that the earlier punishment was worldly.
rows.anchor: أي خسرانا في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational believers should fear repeating the rebellion; believers are singled out as those who benefit from the warning, and ‘a Reminder’ means the Quran.
rows.anchor: أي يا أصحاب العقول ولا تفعلوا مثل ما فعل أولئك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘a Reminder’ means the Messenger, a view also transmitted from Abu Abdillah.
rows.anchor: يعني الرسول عن الحسن وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage links to the prior one by balancing hope with fear: wise people guard against threats, especially since earlier nations were destroyed for disobedience.
rows.anchor: أنه سبحانه بين أن الخوف في مقابلة الرجاء وسبيل العاقل أن يحترز من المخوف

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: One explanation says the garden became like a harvest whose fruit had all been cut away.
rows.anchor: الصريم المصروم ثماره أي المقطوع والمعنى أنها صارت كأن جميع ثمارها قطعت عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another explanation is a place from which all good has been cut off.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الصريم الذي صرم عنه الخير فليس فيه شيء منه عن الحسن

rows.speaker: مؤرج
rows.claim: A third interpretation compares it to sand cut off from the bulk of the dune.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كالصريم أي كالرملة انصرمت عن معظم الرمل عن مؤرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Khuzaymī dialect, it can mean black ashes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كالرماد الأسود بلغة خزيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers called one another in the morning; the term for calling derives from extended voiced sound, as the throat's moisture lets a person's voice carry.
rows.anchor: نادى بعضهم بعضا وقت الصباح وأصل التنادي من الندى بالقصر لأن النداء الدعاء بندي الصوت الذي يمتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their call was to set out early for their crop, meaning their cultivated plants and grapevines, if they intended to harvest the palms.
rows.anchor: والحرث الزروع والأعناب { إن كنتم صارمين } أي قاطعين النخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went off speaking in whispers; the verb comes from the sense of making oneself quiet or hidden.
rows.anchor: يتسارون بينهم وأصله من خفت فلان يخفت إذا أخفى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command that no poor person should enter was the secret they exchanged.
rows.anchor: هذا ما كانوا يتخافتون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They set out intending to keep the poor away, believing they could prevent them and retain the garden's produce.
rows.anchor: { وغدوا على حرد } أي على قصد منع الفقراء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وأبي العالية
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘with resolve’ means they went in earnest and with determination.
rows.anchor: من أمرهم عن مجاهد وقتادة وأبي العالية

rows.speaker: أبي عبيدة
rows.claim: Another view takes it as determined to prevent the poor.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على جد في المنع عن أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Another view says they were angry with the poor.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على حنق وغضب من الفقراء عن سفيان

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Alternatively, they thought themselves able to reach the garden at the time they had planned to cut its crop.
rows.anchor: قادرين مقدرين موافاتهم في الجنة في الوقت الذي قدروا إصرامها فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: On seeing the ruined garden, they first thought they had lost their way and this was not their orchard.
rows.anchor: ضللنا عن الطريق فليس هذا بستاننا عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they had strayed from the right path and were punished for their decision; they then recognized their garden but were deprived of its benefit for denying the poor their share and failing to make an exception.
rows.anchor: إنا لضالون عن الحق في أمرنا فلذلك عوقبنا بذهاب ثمر جنتنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: The ‘middlemost’ brother was the fairest speaker; alternatively, he was the best or wisest, or the one of middle age.
rows.anchor: أي أعدلهم قولا عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The rebuke ‘why do you not glorify?’ means ‘why did you not make an exception?’ because exception acknowledges dependence on God's will.
rows.anchor: قال لولا تستثنون عن مجاهد لأن في الاستثناء التوكل على الله والتعظيم لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations say the rebuke asks why they did not worship and obey God, thank Him by giving the poor their right, acknowledge that God neither does nor approves injustice, or pray.
rows.anchor: هلا تعظمون الله بعبادته واتباع أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admitted wrongdoing in planning to deprive the poor; God is above injustice, so their loss was their own fault, not a wrong done to them.
rows.anchor: في عزمنا على حرمان المساكين من حصتهم عند الصرام فحرمنا قطعها وبالانتفاع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhar and yadaʿ both mean ‘leave’; their wāw-initial forms fell out of use because Arabs disliked beginning a word with wāw, replacing it with other sounds in related words.
rows.anchor: يذر ويدع بمعنى يترك ولا يقال وذر ولا ودع واستغنى بترك عن ذلك لأن الابتداء بالواو عندهم مكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open-vowel naʿma is softness to touch; naʿima can mean wealth or favor, while naʿima with a rounded vowel means happiness.
rows.anchor: والنعمة بفتح النون لين اللمس وضدها الخشونة والنعمة الثروة والمنة أيضا والنعمة بضم النون المسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankāl are shackles; ghussa is a bite stuck in the throat so it cannot pass, also used for an inward choking anguish.
rows.anchor: والأنكال القيود واحدها نكل والغصة تردد اللقمة في الحلق ولا يسيغها آكلها

rows.speaker: عدي بن زيد
rows.claim: His verse about choking without water and a thorny plant shows ghussa as painful choking in the throat.
rows.anchor: لو بغير الماء حلقي شرق كنت كالغصان بالماء اعتصاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kuthayb is a mass of sand; hayl is sand poured so its upper layer flows when its base is moved, as in the cited prophetic expression ‘measure; do not pour.’
rows.anchor: وهلت الرمل أهيله هيلا فهو مهيل إذا حرك أسفله فسال أعلاه

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: Tarafa's line describing a heavy cow witnesses wabil as a thick, weighty club; the same root also describes heavy rain and what is burdensome.
rows.anchor: فمرت كهاة ذات خيف جلالة عقيلة شيخ كالوبيل يلندد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Leave Me and the deniers’ is a threat meaning God will handle requital; ‘people of luxury’ are the wealthy, and the Prophet should not occupy himself with punishing them.
rows.anchor: دعني وإياه إذا أراد أن يهدده وهو نصب على أنه مفعول معه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the short respite ended with Badr and the passage was revealed about ten men who provisioned the enemy there.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل نزلت في المطعمين ببدر وهم عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says it was revealed about Quraysh leaders and those who mocked the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في صناديد قريش والمستهزئين

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: The next life has enormous fetters that can never be unlocked.
rows.anchor: قيودا في الآخرة عظاما لا تفك أبدا عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the fetters as chains; jahim is a name for Hell or a great fire.
rows.anchor: وهو اسم من أسماء جهنم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The choking food has thorns that catch in the throat so nothing enters or leaves; alternatives make it rough food or specifically zaqqum and darīʿ.
rows.anchor: أي ذا شوك يأخذ الحلق فلا يدخل ولا يخرج عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: حمران بن أعين عن عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet heard someone recite this verse and fainted.
rows.anchor: روي عن حمران بن أعين عن عبد الله بن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع قارئا يقرأ هذه فصعق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The mountains become flowing, scattered sand; al-Dahhak explains it as sand that slips beneath a foot and streams above when its base is taken.
rows.anchor: أي رملا سائلا متناثرا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة ويعقوب وخلف
rows.claim: These readers use ‘when the night passes’ without the alif in idh and with the alif in adbara; the other readers use the opposite forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وحمزة ويعقوب وخلف إذ بغير ألف أدبر بالألف والباقون إذا بالألف دبر بغير الألف

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وابن عامر
rows.claim: The Medinese and Ibn Amir read mustanfira with an open fāʾ; the other readers use a kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر مستنفرة بفتح الفاء والباقون بكسر الفاء

rows.speaker: بعضهم عن ابن كثير
rows.claim: An anomalous reading transmitted from Ibn Kathir omits the hamza from ‘one of the greatest.’
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة بعضهم يرويه عن ابن كثير أنها لحد الكبر بلا همزة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr's anomalous reading has the ḥāʾ and nūn unvoweled in ‘spread-out pages.’
rows.anchor: وقراءة سعيد بن جبير صحفا منشرة بسكون الحاء والنون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Dabar and adbar both mean that night has gone away or turned aside.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: والليل إذا أدبر إذا ولى ويقال دبر وأدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightening the hamza makes it intermediate between hamza and a weak consonant; fully omitting it is not regular, though several cited poetic lines attest omission.
rows.anchor: التخفيف في لإحدى الكبر أن يجعل فيها الهمزة بين بين نحو سيم فأما حذف الهمزة فليس بقياس

rows.speaker: أبو الأسود لزياد
rows.claim: The poetic address ‘O father of al-Mughira’ witnesses omission of the hamza in poetic speech.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الأسود لزياد: يا با المغيرة رب أمر معضل

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line on the sin of Atiyya and of the woman who warned him is another example of hamza omission.
rows.anchor: وقال الفرزدق: وعليك إثم عطية بن الخطفي واثم التي زجرتك إن لم تجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra in mustanfira is preferable because ‘fled from a lion’ indicates that the asses themselves were frightened; fatha can instead make the lion or archer frighten them.
rows.anchor: والكسر في مستنفرة أولى لقوله فرت من قسورة فهذا يدل على أنها هي استنفرت

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda takes the open-vowel form to mean frightened.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة مستنفرة مذعورة وأنشد الزجاج

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj adduces a poem describing a donkey following startled asses as evidence for the open-vowel form.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الزجاج: إمسك حمارك إنه مستنفر في إثر أحمرة عمدن لغرب

rows.speaker: ابن سلام
rows.claim: Ibn Sallam recounts Abu Sawwar al-ʿUrani's reading and explanation of the frightened asses, supporting the reading's sense.
rows.anchor: قال ابن سلام سألت أبا سوار العرني وكان أعرابيا فصيحا قارئا للقرآن

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Sukun on the ḥāʾ in ṣuḥuf is a Tamim dialect; the sukun in munshara is justified by common use of nashara cloth and God raising the dead, though the alternative verb is also attested.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني: أما سكون الحاء من صحف فلغة تميمية وأما منشرة بسكون النون فإن العرف في الاستعمال نشرت الثوب

rows.speaker: المتنبي
rows.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's ‘made alive’ line witnesses using ‘spread’ for revived, permitting analogy between a revived corpse and unfolded pages.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء عنهم أيضا نشر الله الميت قال المتنبي: ردت صنائعه إليه حياته

rows.speaker: المتنبي
rows.claim: The line's final word ‘unfolded’ supports describing pages as spread out by analogy with the revived dead.
rows.anchor: فكأنه من نشرها منشور ولم نعلمهم قالوا أنشرت الثوب ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certainty is knowledge that gives the chest a cool feeling of trust; because of this, God is not described as ‘certain.’
rows.anchor: اليقين العلم الذي يوجد برد الثقة به في الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaswara can mean a lion or archers, from a root meaning to overpower.
rows.anchor: والقسورة الأسد. وقيل: هم الرماة من قسرة يقسره قسرا إذا قهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of flight is uncovering or exposing something; the horse is said to flee when it bares its teeth.
rows.anchor: وأصل الفرار الانكشاف عن الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, a sheet that can be turned from one side to another because it bears writing; muṣḥaf derives from the same root.
rows.anchor: والصحف جمع الصحيفة وهي الورقة التي من شأنها أن تقلب من جهة إلى جهة لما فيها من الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘A warner to humankind’ may be a circumstantial participle describing Hell as one of the great calamities, with the feminine referent understood as possessing warning; the masculine form can mean ‘possessing warning.’
rows.anchor: قيل نصب على الحال وهو اسم فاعل بمعنى منذر وذو الحال الضمير في إحدى الكبر العائد إلى الهاء في أنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase attaches to the opening address: ‘O enwrapped one, rise as a warner to humankind.’
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو حال يتعلق بأول السورة فكأنه قال يا أيها المدثر قم نذيرا للبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis reads nadhīr as a verbal noun, ‘warning,’ in the accusative as an object-like cognate accusative.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن النذير هنا بمعنى الإنذار وتقديره إنذارا للبشر فيكون نصبا على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Turning away’ is a circumstantial state from the verbal force of ‘what is the matter with them’; the fleeing-asses clause is another state describing them.
rows.anchor: من معنى الفعل والتقدير أي شيء ثبت لهم معرضين عن التذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla means ‘indeed’; alternatively, it rebuts their assumption that they can overpower the keepers of Hell.
rows.anchor: ليس الأمر على ما يتوهمونه من أنهم يمكنهم دفع خزنة النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is sworn by for the remarkable signs of its rising, setting, course, waxing, and waning.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالقمر لما فيه من الآيات العجيبة في طلوعه وغروبه ومسيره وزيادته ونقصانه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The oath by the night may mean when it goes away; alternatively, dabbara means the night comes after the day and adbara means it departs as morning follows.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة. وقيل: أدبر إذا جاء بعد غيره وأدبر إذا ولى مدبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another view, dabbara and adbara are two dialect forms with the same meaning, to pass away.
rows.anchor: وعلى القول الأول فهما لغتان معناهما ولى وانقضى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The morning is sworn by when it lights up and shines.
rows.anchor: أي إذا أضاء وأنار عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, morning shines by clearing darkness and revealing visible objects; some interpret the oaths as being by the Lord of these things, since an oath may only be made by God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إذا كشف الظلام وأضاء الأشخاص وقال قوم التقدير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: The oath's answer is that Saqar is one of the greatest horrors; alternatively, the Quran's warnings are among the greatest signs.
rows.anchor: يعني أن سقر التي هي النار لإحدى العظائم والكبر جمع الكبرى وهي العظمى عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A warner is a wise guide who alerts people to what they should fear; every prophet warns of God's punishment for disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي منذرا ومخوفا معلما مواضع المخافة والنذير الحكيم بالتحذير عما ينبغي أن يحذر منه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The warner may describe Hell.
rows.anchor: إنه من صفة النار عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Alternatively, the warner is the Prophet, as in the command at the start of the sura to rise and warn.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من صفة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فكأنه قال قم نذيرا عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن رزين
rows.claim: Another view takes the warner as God, with the phrase circumstantial to the omitted oath verb.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من صفة الله تعالى عن ابن رزين وعلى هذا يكون حالا من فعل القسم المحذوف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: To advance or lag behind means to advance in obedience to God or lag through sin; the warning addresses people capable of choosing, contrary to the determinism of the Jabriyya.
rows.anchor: أي يتقدم في طاعة الله أو يتأخر عنها بالمعصية عن قتادة والمشيئة هي الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He is worthy to be feared, so none should be associated with Him; whoever refrains from associating a partner may be forgiven.
rows.anchor: أنا أهل أن أتقى فلا يجعل معي إله فمن اتقى أن يجعل معي إلها فأنا أهل أن أغفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God is the one whose punishment should be feared and to whom people should act obediently so as to earn forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وهو أهل أن يتقى عقابه وأهل أن يعمل له بما يؤدي إلى مغفرته

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: The preceding statement that there is no refuge means there is no fortress.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا حصن عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The final return on that day is to God's judgment and command; no one else can decide or command.
rows.anchor: أي ينتهي الخلق يومئذ إلى حكمه وأمره فلا حكم ولا أمر لأحد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the settlement means the place in which believers and unbelievers reside, and that destination belongs to God rather than worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المستقر المكان الذي يستقر فيه المؤمن والكافر وذلك إلى الله لا إلى العبادة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the settlement the destination and return; it may be temporary or everlasting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المستقر المصير والمرجع عن ابن مسعود والمستقر على وجهين مستقر إلى أمد ومستقر إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: People are told about their earliest and latest deeds.
rows.anchor: يخبر الإنسان يوم القيامة بأول عمله وآخره فيجازي به عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views include deeds begun in life and continued after death, sins committed and duties neglected, what a person did and left, or wealth sent ahead to oneself and wealth left to heirs.
rows.anchor: بما قدم من العمل في حياته وما سنه فعمل به بعد موته من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The report can mean duties a person performed for God and duties delayed and wasted.
rows.anchor: بما قدم من طاعة الله وأخر من حق الله فضيعه عن قتادة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Another view distinguishes property given for oneself from property left to one's heirs.
rows.anchor: بما قدم من ماله لنفسه وما خلفه لورثته بعده عن زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nabaʾ is consequential information; the term fits because only deeds that deserve requital count here, not acts as inconsequential as if they never existed.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة النبأ الخبر بما يعظم شأنه وإنما حسن في هذا الموضع لأن ما جرى مجرى المباح لا يعتد به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومقاتل
rows.claim: The person's own body parts testify to what they did, making the person a witness against themselves.
rows.anchor: أي إن جوارحه تشهد عليه بما عمل فهو شاهد على نفسه بشهادة جوارحه عليه عن ابن عباس وعكرمة ومقاتل

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the body parts stand in for the person, which explains the feminine form; al-Akhfash compares the construction to calling someone a proof or lesson.
rows.anchor: أقام جوارحه مقام نفسه ولذلك أنث لأن المراد بالإنسان ها هنا الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, a person sees themselves and their own deeds clearly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن الإنسان بصير بنفسه وعمله

rows.speaker: محمد بن مسلم عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah says there is no use appearing good while concealing evil, because a person knows on returning to themselves that the outward and inward do not match.
rows.anchor: ما يصنع أحدكم أن يظهر حسنا ويسر سيئا أليس إذا رجع إلى نفسه يعلم أنه ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: عمر بن يزيد عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah says one cannot justify oneself to people contrary to what God knows; he quotes the Prophet as teaching that a sound inner life strengthens outward conduct.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو بكر عن عاصم والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce tanwin on salāsil and both occurrences of qawārīr, adding alif when pausing on each.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وأبو بكر عن عاصم والكسائي { سلاسلا } بالتنوين وكذلك قواريرا ويقفون بالألف على الجميع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وخلف
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Khalaf omit tanwin on salāsil, retain it on the first qawārīr but not the second, and pause without alif on salāsil and the second qawārīr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وخلف سلاسل بغير تنوين وقواريرا قوارير الأول بالتنوين والثاني بغير تنوين

rows.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
rows.claim: Hamza and Yaʿqub omit tanwin throughout and pause without alif on all these words.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ويعقوب بغير تنوين في الجميع ويقفان بغير ألف عليها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص
rows.claim: They omit tanwin, but use pausal alif for salāsil and the first qawārīr, not the second; Shuʿja also omits that alif on salāsil.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص بغير تنوين فيها أيضا إلا أنهم يقفون على سلاسل وقواريرا الأولى بالألف

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Some Arabs decline normally indeclinable words; poetic habit can extend that usage to prose, tolerating added tanwin as poets tolerate metrical addition or deletion.
rows.anchor: سمعنا من العرب من يصرف هذا ويصرف جميع ما لا ينصرف قال وهذه لغة أهل الشعر

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: The plurals also resemble declinable singulars because they are formed like ordinary plurals; the forms ṣawāḥibāt and mawaliyāt illustrate this analogy.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الجموع أشبهت الآحاد لأنهم قالوا صواحبات يوسف فلما جمعت جمع الآحاد المنصرفة جعلوه في حكمها

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line about men bowing their heads illustrates this declension pattern in a plural.
rows.anchor: وأنشد للفرزدق: فإذا الرجال رأوا يزيد رأيتهم خضع الرقاب نواكس الأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers without tanwin treat the forms like the coordinated list in the verse about monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques; pausal alif parallels Quranic alifs at verse endings.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بغير تنوين ولا ألف فإنه جعله كقوله لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahr is the passage of night and day; its plurals include adhur and duhur.
rows.anchor: الدهر مرور الليل والنهار وجمعه أدهر ودهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nuṭfa is a small amount of water but can also denote a large amount; Ali used it for the Nahrawan battlefield and poetry gives an example.
rows.anchor: وأصل النطفة الماء القليل وقد تقع على الكثير

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: Ali called the Kharijites' battlefield ‘beyond the nuṭfa,’ meaning the Nahrawan river.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين ع حين ذكر الخوارج: مصارعهم دون النطفة يريد النهروان

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: The line comparing the soul to a drop in a basin shows nuṭfa can mean a small quantity of fluid.
rows.anchor: وما النفس إلا نطفة بقرارة إذا لم تكدر كان صفوا غديرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshāj means mixtures and is the plural of mashīj or mashj; to mix one thing with another is to mashaja it.
rows.anchor: وواحد الأمشاج مشيج ومشجت هذا بهذا أي خلطته وهو ممشوج ومشيج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrār can be the plural of bārr, like nāṣir/nṣār, or a plural of barr.
rows.anchor: وواحد الأبرار بار نحو ناصر وأنصار وبر أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cup is a drinking vessel once it contains a drink.
rows.anchor: والكأس الإناء إذا كان فيه شراب

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: His verse about Um ʿAmr's cup witnesses kās as a vessel containing wine.
rows.anchor: صددت الكأس عنا أم عمرو وكان الكأس مجراها اليمينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awfā is the Hijazi form; waffā is used by Tamim and Najd.
rows.anchor: وأوفى بالعقد ووفى به فأوفى لغة أهل الحجاز ووفى لغة تميم وأهل نجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow is a binding deed a person obligates themselves to perform.
rows.anchor: والنذر عقد عملي فعل بر يوجبه الإنسان على نفسه نذر ينذر

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antara's line describes opponents vowing to kill him if they meet, illustrating the use of nadhr for a vow.
rows.anchor: الشاتمي عرضي ولم أشتمهما والناذرين إذا لم ألقهما دمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustatīr means spreading or becoming widespread.
rows.anchor: والمستطير المنتشر

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line about a spreading wound in the heart witnesses the meaning of mustatīr.
rows.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
فبانت وقد أسأرت في الفؤ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qamṭarīr describes extreme hardship, as if evil is tightly twisted together; the word also appears as qamṭar.
rows.anchor: والقمطرير الشديد في الشر وقد اقمطر اليوم اقمطرارا ويوم قمطرير وقماطر كأنه قد التف شره بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: The line asking cousins to remember a severe day illustrates qamṭar as a description of distress.
rows.anchor: بني عمنا هل تذكرون بلأنا عليكم إذا ما كان يوم قماطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited usage, hal can mean qad, ‘already.’
rows.anchor: إن هل هنا بمعنى قد

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: The poetic question whether an old person has wept his full tear illustrates hal with the sense ‘already.’
rows.anchor: أم هل كبير بكى لم يقض عبرته إثر الأحبة يوم البين مشكوم

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن ميمون عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: A report says Ali and Fatima gave all their barley porridge in thirds to a poor person, an orphan, and a captive who each asked for help, without eating any themselves; the verses were revealed about them and apply to every believer who does likewise sincerely.
rows.anchor: كان عند فاطمة شعير فجعلوه عصيدة فلما أنضجوها ووضعوها بين أيديهم جاء مسكين فقال المسكين رحمكم الله

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
rows.claim: Abu Hamza says the whole sura is Medinan and was revealed about Ali and Fatima.
rows.anchor: أبو حمزة الثمالي في تفسيره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas gives a sequence of Meccan revelations and says those listed were eighty-five Meccan suras, offering an alternative chronology to the Medinan reports.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما أنزل بمكة
